content.comment_body: Hello, is there a way to use the current time? It's stored in bytes 984-990 of the VM area. I need to transfer this data to a MODBUS device, but no available block offers a parameter for this mapping to the VM area. Does anyone have ideas?
The real-time clock's current time is found in bytes 984-990 of the VM area, not blocks. It's not accessible from within a [product_name] program.
Hello, I realize now it's the VM area, not a block—my mistake. I was considering if any program block could make the current time available for mapping within VM memory.
The current time exists within the VM area. Although I haven't worked with MODBUS, could it be possible to read these VM addresses from the MODBUS side?
Hello, I need to write the time data via MODBUS—basically, to organize it into a block for mapping the time units and then forward the VM mapping to MODBUS.
It's not possible to map these bytes, since parameter-based VM mapping does not provide access.

analysis.insight_summary: The conversation highlights the challenge of accessing and mapping current time data (bytes 984-990 in the VM area) to MODBUS using [product_name] devices. Users express concern over the lack of a direct method for sharing system time externally, exposing usability issues in how parameter mapping is currently configured.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish to directly access and map real-time clock data from the device's memory to blocks available for MODBUS communication, enabling the transfer of time data to external systems.
